textbookText: Figure: 9.2.5 Earwig showing positive thigmotaxis Figure: 9.2.6 Fruit flies showing negative geotaxis 5. Geotaxis: It is the response of organism to Earth’s gravity. Earthworm always tends to move downward away from earth surface indicating positive geotaxis. Paramecium responds by swimming up in water against gravity which is negative geotaxis. Fruit fly also move up if kept in a vertical glass tube. Arboreal animals show negative geotaxis whereas animals living underground show positive geotaxis. 6. Rheotaxis: Movement of animals in response to water and air current is called rheotaxis. Some fishes like eel avoid oncoming water currents and turn away where as some fish like zebra fish move towards the current of water. Birds and insects show positive rheotaxis although they can move in any direction.
